verdict.rationale: The product is a set of skill files that the installer 'writes into your repo as ordinary files you own and can edit,' with 'nothing updates behind your back' and an explicit MIT license — i.e., the entire core product can be self-hosted as local files with no server dependency, and updates are pulled explicitly via `npx skills update` rather than pushed. This directly satisfies the self-host/openness axis for an AI-native user who wants to own and control the artifact. Missing for 10: no independent/hands-on report specifically confirming self-hosted operation works end-to-end, and no discussion of air-gapped/offline usage guarantees.
